title: SMUD Rebates 2026: Every Amount, Updated
desc: Every SMUD home rebate in 2026: heat pump $1,000 to $3,000, water heater $3,000 to $4,000, Go Electric up to $4,000, EV charger up to $850, battery $300 per kWh, induction $750.
lead: This post said SMUD pays up to $600 for an EV charger. SMUD's page now says up to $850, and several other figures changed. Everything below was read from SMUD's pages on October 2, 2026. SMUD's rebates depend on funding, so confirm before you buy.
sections: Every SMUD rebate at a glance

• Heat pump HVAC: $3,000 variable-stage and $2,000 two-stage (15.2 SEER2 minimum) replacing gas; $1,000 upgrading from electric.
  • Heat pump water heater: $3,000 (50 gallons or more), $3,500 (65 or more), $4,000 (80 or more) replacing gas; $1,000 replacing electric. NEEA Tier III or IV, UEF 2.87 or higher.
  • Go Electric (panel, subpanel, circuit): up to $4,000, with a gas-to-electric conversion required for the subpanel and circuit.
  • Seal and insulate: up to $3,000 through a Home Performance Program contractor.
  • EV charger (Charge@Home): up to $850: charger up to $100, circuit sharing device up to $200, circuit installation up to $750.
  • Battery: $300 per kWh up to $6,000 from September 23, 2026 ($500 per kWh up to $10,000 for projects submitted by September 22 and enrolled by December 31).
  • Induction cooking: $750 from gas, $100 from electric. Smart thermostat: $50 at the SMUD Energy Store.

SMUD publishes median installed prices from its own customers: $18,804 for a gas-to-electric heat pump and $6,220 for a gas-to-electric heat pump water heater, before rebates. See Sacramento rebates for the full pages.

Heat pumps, water heaters and insulation are claimed by a contractor in the SMUD Contractor Network, who submits the rebate for you. The EV rebate has its own application and wants the vehicle registered at your SMUD address in your name. One Charge@Home rebate per account for life.
faq: How much does SMUD pay for an EV charger?
Up to $850: up to $100 for the charger, up to $200 for a circuit sharing device and up to $750 for the circuit.
Did the SMUD battery rebate change?
Yes. For interconnection applications from September 23, 2026 it is $300 per kWh up to $6,000.
Do I need a SMUD contractor?
For heat pumps, water heaters and insulation, yes.
